what_happened: The job asked to keep read requests in the plan and drain queue. It was rejected. The verifier failed 1 of 6 acceptance criteria. The unmet criterion said read requests on non-drained channels, running or closed jobs, and declined jobs must not enter the queue, with a test for each, and that cargo test, clippy and fmt pass. There were three blocker or major findings. (1) The default --budget 2 symptom was not checked or fixed, and the plan's room check is wrong: it reserves room for a run that plan never makes (drain.rs, Drain::prepare, called by plan). (2) Criterion 4 has no tests for a read request on a non-drained channel, or for running and closed jobs going through queued_work (steward.rs tests). (3) The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met. No failed checks are listed.
cause: Nothing cross-checks the accepted reading against the request's stated symptom before the build starts. The request evidently named a symptom (the budget behavior) that the reading dropped or reframed. The criteria were then written from the reading, so passing them proved nothing about the request. Nothing required each exclusion in a criterion to map to a named test, and nothing compared the build's tests to the criteria before handover. Both gaps surfaced only at the final verdict. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the request text or the reading.
prevention: Add a reading-admission check that lists every symptom, outcome and exclusion in the request as a numbered item. Each item must map to at least one acceptance criterion, or be explicitly marked out of scope and shown to the user. Add a pre-handover check that every criterion calling for tests names a test per case (for example one per excluded kind), and that each named test exists and passes. This catches reading drift early and covers missing per-case tests.
proposed_request: Fix the plan and drain queue so that read requests stay in it. First, reproduce the default `--budget 2` symptom and fix it. In particular, make the plan's room check in Drain::prepare (called by plan) reserve room only for runs that plan actually makes. Keep these out of the queue, with one named test for each: read requests on channels other than the drained ones, jobs that are running or closed, and declined jobs. Add the missing tests for a read request on a non-drained channel, and for running and closed jobs going through queued_work in steward.rs. Add a test that plan with the default budget keeps read requests. Before handover, confirm that every item in this request maps to a criterion and a passing test. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` must pass.
